glassSubstrates.name: Lithium Aluminosilicate Glass-Ceramic (LAS - Schott Ceran / EuroKera)
glassSubstrates.description: Engineered zero-expansion glass-ceramic containing microscopic high-quartz solid solution nanocrystals (70–75 nm). The negative thermal expansion of the crystal phase cancels out the positive thermal expansion of the residual vitreous silica phase, yielding an effective coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE) of virtually zero (0.05 × 10^-6 /K). Impervious to bulk thermal shock, but remains vulnerable to localized point-load contact stress and high-temperature sucrose/fructose chemical pitting.

glassSubstrates.name: Thermally Tempered Soda-Lime Silicate Glass
glassSubstrates.description: Standard float glass pre-stressed via rapid air quenching. Possesses a high thermal expansion coefficient (8.8 × 10^-6 /K) and a catastrophic thermal shock threshold of only ΔT ≈ 120°C–140°C. If cold water (10°C) overflows from a boiling pot onto a burner surface reaching 220°C, the sudden tensile surface stress exceeds the compressive tempering envelope, triggering explosive fragmentation into thousands of blunt dices.

glassSubstrates.name: Chemically Strengthened Aluminosilicate Glass
glassSubstrates.description: Aluminosilicate glass treated in a molten potassium salt bath (KNO3 at 450°C), replacing smaller surface sodium ions with larger potassium ions to establish an ultra-dense compressive stress layer (depth of layer 50–70 µm, surface compression >750 MPa). Highly resistant to heavy pot drops and surface scratches, though continuous acoustic high-frequency vibrations can initiate sub-surface micro-crack fatigue.

glassSubstrates.name: Micro-Crystalline Cordierite Ceramic Plate
glassSubstrates.sugarPittingVulnerability: Very Low (Resistant to Molten Sugar Pitting)
glassSubstrates.description: Opaque high-density magnesium aluminum silicate ceramic (2MgO·2Al2O3·5SiO2) engineered for heavy-duty commercial restaurant ranges. Possesses high fracture toughness and superior acoustic damping, resisting continuous 20 kHz magnetostrictive chattering without interfacial delamination.

cookwareInterfaces.name: 3-Ply / 5-Ply Multiclad Stainless Steel (Magnetic Base + Aluminum Core)
cookwareInterfaces.description: Composite pan construction with magnetic 430/439 ferritic stainless steel base bonded to an inner aluminum conductive core. Due to the severe differential thermal expansion between aluminum (23 × 10^-6 /K) and ferritic steel (10.5 × 10^-6 /K), high heat causes the bottom to bow convexly or concavely, lifting the pan edges and concentrating the entire mechanical load onto small ring or center contact points.

cookwareInterfaces.name: Heavy Enameled Cast Iron Dutch Oven (4.5–7.0 kg)
cookwareInterfaces.description: Massive ferromagnetic body providing exceptional magnetic field coupling and induction efficiency. However, its high static weight (up to 7 kg loaded) combined with a rough vitreous enamel bottom generates extreme localized contact pressures. If dragged across microscopic quartz sand grains or salt crystals on the glass, it produces deep surface gouges that act as critical Griffith fracture notches.

cookwareInterfaces.name: Severely Warped / Concave Defective Base (1.5mm Air Gap)
cookwareInterfaces.description: Cookware whose base has buckled from previous cold water quenching. The 1.5mm central air gap prevents uniform conductive heat transfer from the pan back into the cooktop thermistor sensor. The induction coil continues pumping full wattage into the peripheral contact ring, driving severe localized thermal gradients (>160°C/cm) and intense acoustic cavity resonance.

cookwareInterfaces.name: Stamped Ferritic Dot / Mesh Plate on Cast Aluminum
cookwareInterfaces.description: Die-cast aluminum frying pan with a perforated magnetic stainless steel plate cold-pressed into the bottom. The discontinuous magnetic dots create localized electromagnetic eddy current hotspots, rapid differential expansion, and audible high-frequency chattering at the glass-metal interface.

thermalTransientScenarios.name: Power Boost Dry Pan Thermal Surge (3,700W • 20°C → 280°C in 30s)
thermalTransientScenarios.description: An empty pan placed on an active induction burner with 'Boost' mode activated (3.2 kW – 3.7 kW). Without a food water matrix to absorb the latent heat of vaporization, the pan base accelerates to nearly 300°C in under 30 seconds. The glass directly beneath the contact ring heats rapidly while surrounding glass remains at 25°C, establishing massive shear stress across the boundary.

thermalTransientScenarios.name: Boiling Pan Searing Overflow onto Hot Glass (240°C Pan + 10°C Water)
thermalTransientScenarios.description: A pan searing at 240°C experiences a sudden cold water or frozen broth boil-over. Water at 10°C cascades onto the glowing hot cooktop surface. In soda-lime glass, the rapid thermal contraction of the upper surface creates instantaneous tensile stresses exceeding 200 MPa, triggering catastrophic fracture.

thermalTransientScenarios.name: Molten Sugar / Jam Boil-Over & Chemical Glaze Pitting (180°C Pyrolysis)
thermalTransientScenarios.description: Sucrose, caramel, or fruit jam boils over onto the hot burner zone. Above 160°C, sucrose melts and pyrolyzes. The organic acids and hydroxyl groups chemically fuse to the silicate tetrahedral network of the glass-ceramic. As the sugar cools, its high coefficient of thermal contraction pulls out chunks of glass ('pitting' or spallation).

thermalTransientScenarios.name: Equilibrium Water Simmer (800W • 95°C Steady State)
thermalTransientScenarios.description: Gentle simmering of soups or stews with 800W continuous modulation. Water phase equilibrium regulates the pan base temperature strictly below 105°C, maintaining negligible thermal stress.

acousticResonanceModes.name: Dual Burner Inverter Frequency Mismatch (Beat Frequency: 1–3 kHz Whine)
acousticResonanceModes.description: Occurs when two adjacent burners share a dual-inverter module operating at slightly mismatched resonant frequencies (e.g., 24.0 kHz and 25.2 kHz). The heterodyne beat frequency (1,200 Hz) falls squarely in the audible human hearing range and creates an interfacial microscopic vibrating shear between pan and glass.

acousticResonanceModes.name: 120 Hz Magnetostrictive Cookware Base Flexing & Buzz
acousticResonanceModes.description: The alternating magnetic field induces physical strain (magnetostriction) in the ferromagnetic pan base, expanding and contracting the iron crystal lattice twice per electrical mains cycle (100 Hz in 50Hz grids, 120 Hz in 60Hz grids). The pan bottom taps against the glass 120 times per second.

acousticResonanceModes.name: Single-Coil Pure Ultrasonic Modulation (>32 kHz - Silent & Smooth)
acousticResonanceModes.description: Modern full-bridge inverter operating above 32 kHz beyond the human hearing limit and above the structural resonant frequency of most multi-ply cookware. Minimal interfacial shear stress.

surfaceDefectStates.name: Pristine Factory Glass Surface (Ra < 0.05 µm, No Micro-Notches)
surfaceDefectStates.description: Factory-fresh smooth surface with intact surface compressive layer. Griffith critical crack length is orders of magnitude larger than existing nano-imperfections.

surfaceDefectStates.name: Surface Scratches & Abrasions (Sand Grit / Salt Dragging, Depth 25 µm)
surfaceDefectStates.description: Visible fine scratches caused by sliding rough cookware bases over salt granules or abrasive scouring pads. Micro-notches concentrate applied thermal and mechanical tensile stresses by 3.4x.

surfaceDefectStates.name: Sub-Surface Micro-Cracks & Thermal Fatigue Crazing (Depth 75 µm)
surfaceDefectStates.description: Severe sub-surface fissures resulting from previous cookware edge drops or repeated thermal shocks. Griffith stress threshold is dramatically reduced; small thermal transients can initiate catastrophic runaway crack propagation.
